stemMd: A company suspects that confusing invoice codes cause customers to pay late. It plans to replace codes with plain-language descriptions. Which finding most supports the prediction that this change will reduce late payment?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The company’s logo was redesigned last year.

options.label: B
options.textMd: In a randomized trial, otherwise identical invoices with plain descriptions were paid earlier than coded invoices.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Several customers buy more than one product.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Plain descriptions occupy more page space.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Late payment can create cash-flow problems.

explanationMd: The randomized comparison changes the proposed feature while holding other invoice information constant, supplying direct evidence for the intended causal effect.

distractorRationale.a: The logo change is not evidence about the proposed descriptions.
distractorRationale.d: Page space alone does not link wording to payment timing.
distractorRationale.e: This shows why the issue matters, not whether the proposed remedy works.
distractorRationale.c: Product count does not isolate the effect of invoice wording.
